EPA Plans to Allow Unlimited Dumping of Fracking Wastewater in the Gulf of Mexico

I know a bit about fracking, and this is something that has bothered me for a while.

It's possible to frack with liquid nitrogen instead of diesel fuel (yes, most fracking fluid is diesel fuel mixed with whatever proprietary chemicals a company wants to put in). Liquid nitrogen is more expensive than diesel fuel, which is probably a good reason for companies to use diesel fuel instead. That's the case until you look at how much cleanup costs. Liquid nitrogen cleanup = wait for liquid nitrogen to boil off (our atmosphere is ~ 70% nitrogen). Diesel fuel cleanup = build retention ponds, and spend a shit ton of money to sequester the waste, or otherwise break it down to less bad waste products. At the end of the day using either diesel fuel, or liquid nitrogen come out to around the same costs... so long as you actually do the cleanup.

There are few companies using liquid nitrogen. The industry standard is diesel fuel. I think that most people are skimping on cleanup to save costs, and I think that our regulatory bodies are implicit in this.
